title: A Starfish With 21 Arms Eats 10 Square Metres of Coral a Year

scenes.text: Divers on this reef carry syringes of vinegar.
They're hunting a starfish with up to 21 arms, 80 centimetres across, and hundreds of toxin-tipped spines.
scenes.keywords: crown of thorns starfish on coral

scenes.text: It climbs onto living coral, pushes its stomach out through its mouth, and digests the coral where it stands.
scenes.keywords: crown of thorns starfish eating coral

scenes.text: One adult eats up to 10 square metres of coral a year. One big female releases over 200 million eggs.
scenes.keywords: crown of thorns starfish close up spines

scenes.text: In an outbreak they can kill up to 90 percent of the corals on a reef.
One injection of vinegar or bile salts kills it. So the divers swim, and stab. Starfish by starfish.

description:
The crown-of-thorns starfish has up to 21 arms, grows to 80 cm across, and feeds by pushing its stomach out through its mouth onto living coral.
One adult can eat up to 10 square metres of coral a year, a large female releases over 200 million eggs, and outbreaks can kill up to 90 percent of the corals on a reef, so divers on the Great Barrier Reef cull them with a single injection of vinegar or bile salts.
Should we be killing one animal to save another?

first_comment: Its spines carry toxins that can damage your liver, and a single starfish eats about 20 cm of coral every night. Would you volunteer to dive and inject them?
